judgments.note: Municipal appeal of a PUD denial is clear. Housing rests on the 6-unit senior residence (multiple family dwelling, or at worst assisted living, a care home) within a mixed-use PUD; documents do not say whether it is new construction or a conversion of the former school, but either creates housing.
Same as disposition; the six visitor residences/dormitory are letting rooms, not counted.
6-unit Senior Citizen Residence; the court flagged it might instead be assisted living. Dormitory/visitor residences excluded as rooms let.

The court calls SEVCA and The Community Alliance 'two additional appellants' alongside the Applicant, though they were not applicants below; classed as developer since they would own and operate the project.
The appellants' grounds against the PUD denial are never described; Town Plan conformance is a standard, not an observed contention.
Final order entered the docket as CONCLUDED; the remand is for municipal consideration of an amended application and reopening is only a possibility, so resolved.
The Planning Commission denial was never reversed; the court remanded without deciding the merits.
The court states this is a de novo proceeding and that both applications, including 208-12-01, will be addressed on their merits; it held an evidentiary hearing.
